clue.text: Notepaper?

parts.note: read not as writing paper but as paper printed with musical notes for a player to read

explanation.surface: A one-word query about stationery for jotting memos.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed music is literally paper carrying notes, the written symbols of pitch and duration.

clue.text: Panic, getting accommodation on the nail

parts.note: flats are a form of housing or accommodation
a pin is a small slender nail

explanation.surface: Someone panics on finding lodgings available immediately, on the nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the nail' looks like one idiom (paid promptly), but 'on' just joins the pieces and 'nail' alone gives PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat spin is an idiom for a state of agitated panic, from an aircraft spinning out of control.

clue.text: When women's dress is lifted in divine residence?

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting something turns it upward, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by men

explanation.surface: A naughty picture of skirts being raised inside a holy abode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Women's dress' looks like a dress worn by women; it means DRAG, which read upwards gives GARD.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth this is the realm where the gods live, a dwelling of the divine.

clue.text: Discharge great quantities heavenward

indicators.note: going up towards the sky, so in a down clue the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: tons is informal for great quantities, as in 'tons of food'

explanation.surface: Something spews out large amounts skyward, like a geyser.
explanation.definitionFit: Mucus from the nose is a bodily discharge, given here by its slang name.

clue.text: Couple can't be converted to the work of Gilbert and George, say

definitions.text: the work of Gilbert and George, say
definitions.note: the definition describes a kind of art, matched by the adjective as in 'conceptual art'

indicators.note: converting something changes its form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pair who refuse to be won over to the art of a famous duo.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and George are a British artist duo, and 'Couple' in the surface seems to echo them; it is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and George are known for idea-driven art, an example of the conceptual art movement.

clue.text: Panoramic primrose, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a ... view is one seen from high above, taking in the whole panorama
the ... primrose is a small pink wild primrose, one of several plants so named

explanation.surface: A description of a sweeping view of a pale yellow flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a wide overhead view and also names a primrose species, two separate senses.

clue.text: Force invading state, but meaning no harm

indicators.note: one piece goes into another, as an army entering a country

parts.note: Benin is a West African state
G is the symbol for gravitational force in physics

explanation.surface: An army enters a country, yet claims to come in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' suggests a condition; here it is the country BENIN, which G enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindly and harmless is the sense of the adjective, used of people who mean well.

clue.text: Sticks up, self-satisfied

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: gums are adhesives, things that stick

explanation.surface: Someone smug sticks their nose up, sure of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' looks like a verb or twigs; read as a noun it is GUMS, glues that stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugness is complacent self-satisfaction, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Doesn't release senior and junior model trapped in house

indicators.note: these pieces are shut inside the abbreviation as if imprisoned

parts.note: old means elder or senior
a son is a junior family member, as Jr after a name
the Model T was Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: A father and son and a model are held captive in a house and not released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Senior and junior' looks like a pair of people, but the words give separate pieces, both shut inside the abbreviation for house along with the car.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep hold of something is the opposite of letting it go, a plain synonym phrase.

clue.text: Part of inner tube, or of erstwhile umbrella?

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words that follows, spanning the word boundary

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about bits of an old bicycle tube or a former umbrella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inner tube' suggests a tyre; it means the body's internal tube, the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: The ileum is the final section of the small intestine, a tube inside the body.

clue.text: Selected portion of old publication

parts.note: ex- means former or old, as in ex-wife
a tract is a short published pamphlet

explanation.surface: An excerpt taken from a long-defunct pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract is a passage picked out of a larger work, so a chosen portion.

clue.text: Two fish for an apple

parts.note: the cod is a familiar food fish
the ling is another fish, of the cod family

explanation.surface: A seemingly strange trade of a pair of fish for a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two fish' supplies both pieces, one fish each; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A codling is a variety of cooking apple, elongated and sharp-tasting.

clue.text: Lambretta-rider taking exercise on one?

indicators.note: one piece takes in the other, holding it inside

parts.note: a Mod, a member of the 1960s British youth subculture, typically rode a Lambretta scooter
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A 1960s scooter fan exercising while astride the machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' points back to the Lambretta itself, the kind of motorised two-wheeler that is the answer; Mods were a 1960s British youth subculture famed for riding them.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lambretta is a light motorised two-wheeler, the kind of machine meant here as an example.

clue.text: The men put out first? Far from it

indicators.note: put out can mean disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about which team goes in to bat first, answered with a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as one phrase meaning dismissed; 'put' is fodder and 'out' alone signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming after countless others is about as far from first in a sequence as possible.

clue.text: Firm brown digit set before novelist

indicators.note: the brown and digit pieces are placed ahead of the firm piece

parts.note: umber is a brown earth pigment
a toe is a digit of the foot
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A company of brown-toed workers puts a writer in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian author of The Name of the Rose was a celebrated novelist and semiotician.

clue.text: Skid, sounding drunk, and collapse on the road

indicators.note: the word is said aloud and only its sound is used

parts.note: high means intoxicated
to drop is to fall or collapse
a lane is a narrow road

explanation.surface: A drunk driver skids and slumps onto the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounding' applies only to 'drunk'; 'on the' are linking words before 'road'.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydroplane is to aquaplane, a vehicle skidding on a film of water.

clue.text: Film of girl catching Poles' disease and musical couple taking composer aback

indicators.note: the name holds the poles inside it

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
N and S are the north and south poles
TB is tuberculosis

indicators.note: the whole combined piece is read backwards
the musical pair holds the composer inside

parts.note: a duo is a pair of musicians
Ravel was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: A girl falls ill while a musical duo plays a composer backwards, all in one movie.
explanation.walkthrough: DUO taking RAVEL gives DRAVELUO; 'aback' turns it to OULEVARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Wilder's 1950 Hollywood classic about a faded silent star is the film named.

clue.text: Before receiving shock treatment, I left — that may be raised

indicators.note: the first word takes the others inside it

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before
ECT is electroconvulsive therapy

explanation.surface: A patient left before getting electric shocks, in a deadpan medical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That may be raised' is the definition, describing tissue or a crest able to stand up; 'receiving' wraps the first word round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Erectile tissue or a crest can be made upright, so the adjective means able to be raised.

clue.text: Material decrees to restrict yobs swamping the east of France

indicators.note: the orders engulf the French word, which ends up inside them

parts.note: ASBOs were anti-social behaviour orders, British court orders curbing troublemakers
est is French for east

explanation.surface: Court orders against hooligans overwhelm eastern France.
explanation.walkthrough: ASBOs were UK court orders against antisocial behaviour; 'the east of France' looks like the last letter of France but is the French word EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral used as a fireproof building material.

clue.text: Animal doctor interrupts cure in place of worship

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: the doctor breaks into the middle of the cure word

parts.note: to heal is to cure

explanation.surface: A vet barges in on a healing session inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal doctor' reads as a vet, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a large church, the seat of a bishop, so a place of worship.

clue.text: Headgear that's initially talk of the town

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: urban means relating to a town or city

explanation.surface: A hat that becomes the talk of the town.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a length of cloth wound round the head, a type of headwear.

clue.text: Hunchback with mouth odour

parts.note: gob is British slang for mouth
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A hunched figure with bad breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbo is Italian for hunchback, and Launcelot Gobbo is a character in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Writer on 1, topless, talking incoherently

definitions.note: 1-down is printed music, so a writer of it is a composer

indicators.note: the remaining letters are jumbled as in muddled speech
losing the top means dropping the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A writer rambling half-naked and making no sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes T from TALKING, leaving ALKING, which 'incoherently' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a 19th-century Russian composer, someone who writes music.

clue.text: Get down to work keeping time right in musical passage

indicators.note: the phrase holds the two letters inside it

parts.note: to set to is to start working in earnest

explanation.surface: Musicians start rehearsing, staying strictly in tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: SET TO opens after S to take T and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretto is a passage, especially in a fugue, where entries overlap at shorter intervals.

clue.text: Piece of furniture to date inconclusively

indicators.note: without its conclusion, so the final letter goes

parts.note: so far means up to now

explanation.surface: A dating attempt on a couch that ends without result.
explanation.definitionFit: A sofa is an upholstered seat for several people, a familiar furnishing.

clue.text: That's one fewer sent back as scrap

parts.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, meaning that is or namely
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: the word is returned the other way, read backwards

parts.note: less means fewer

explanation.surface: Something returned with one item missing is written off as junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is SC, the scholarly abbreviation for 'namely'; only LESS is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissel is the metal clippings left over from stamping coins, a form of scrap.

clue.text: Expressed contempt for minor altercation

explanation.surface: Scorn shown during a small squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a past tense of spit, a gesture of contempt, and also a noun for a trivial row.

clue.text: Don't pass round the trainee's weapon!

indicators.note: the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: to fail is not to pass a test
L is for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A warning not to hand round a trainee's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass round' looks like a phrase; 'round' is the container indicator. L-plates mark British learner drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A flail is a threshing tool also used as a medieval weapon with a swinging head.

clue.text: Depressed by drug prevention campaign

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: Someone low from drug use, facing a police clampdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, a link word; the drug piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a firm campaign to stop or suppress an activity.
